clinician_landing.seo_title: Best Digital Tools for Mental Health Clinicians 2026 | HeyPsych
clinician_landing.meta_description: Evidence-based tools for mental health clinicians: AI scribes, clinical decision support, billing tools, EHRs, and patient engagement platforms reviewed by our medical board.
clinician_landing.direct_answer: The best tools for mental health clinicians include AI-powered documentation assistants like DeepScribe, clinical evidence platforms like OpenEvidence, specialized EHRs like PracticeQ, and patient engagement apps. These tools reduce administrative burden and improve care quality.
clinician_landing.intro: Mental health clinicians face unique workflow challenges. We've reviewed the best digital tools to help with documentation, clinical decision-making, billing, practice management, and patient engagement between sessions.

faqs.q: What is the best AI scribe for mental health clinicians?
faqs.a: The best AI scribes for mental health include DeepScribe and similar ambient documentation tools that can generate SOAP notes from therapy sessions. Look for tools specifically trained on mental health encounters and those with strong HIPAA compliance.

faqs.q: What EHR is best for therapists and psychiatrists?
faqs.a: PracticeQ, SimplePractice, and TherapyNotes are popular EHRs designed for mental health practices. The best choice depends on your practice size, whether you need telehealth integration, and billing requirements.

faqs.q: Are AI tools safe to use in clinical practice?
faqs.a: AI tools can be safe when properly implemented. Look for HIPAA compliance, BAA availability, clear documentation of AI limitations, and always maintain clinical oversight. AI should augment, not replace, clinical judgment.

faqs.q: What tools help with psychiatric medication decisions?
faqs.a: Clinical decision support tools like OpenEvidence, UpToDate, and specialized pharmacology references help with medication selection and interaction checking. These should complement, not replace, clinical training and judgment.

faqs.q: How can I reduce documentation time as a therapist?
faqs.a: AI scribes, voice-to-text tools, and structured note templates can significantly reduce documentation time. Some clinicians report saving 1-2 hours daily with ambient documentation assistants.

faqs.q: What tools help with patient engagement between sessions?
faqs.a: Apps like Woebot, Wysa, and mood trackers can supplement therapy by providing between-session support and homework. Look for tools that allow you to monitor patient progress or assign specific exercises.

faqs.q: Do I need special tools for telehealth?
faqs.a: Most modern EHRs include HIPAA-compliant telehealth. Standalone options include Doxy.me and Zoom for Healthcare. Consider integration with your existing workflow and billing capabilities.

faqs.q: What billing tools work for mental health practices?
faqs.a: Mental health billing has unique requirements (therapy codes, prior auth, carve-outs). Look for billing tools or clearinghouses familiar with behavioral health like Availity, Office Ally, or built-in EHR billing.

hubs.seo_title: Clinical Evidence & Decision Support Tools for Clinicians 2026 | HeyPsych
hubs.meta_description: Find answers fast with clinical evidence tools. OpenEvidence, UpToDate alternatives, and AI-powered clinical decision support for mental health professionals.
hubs.direct_answer: Clinical evidence tools like OpenEvidence provide instant, AI-powered answers to clinical questions using peer-reviewed literature. These tools help clinicians make evidence-based decisions quickly during patient encounters.
hubs.intro: When you need answers fast during a patient encounter, these tools search peer-reviewed literature and clinical guidelines to provide evidence-based recommendations. Designed for busy clinicians who need reliable information in seconds.

faqs.q: What is OpenEvidence?
faqs.a: OpenEvidence is an AI-powered clinical decision support tool that provides evidence-based answers to clinical questions. It searches peer-reviewed literature and synthesizes answers with citations, designed for use during patient encounters.

faqs.q: Is OpenEvidence free for clinicians?
faqs.a: OpenEvidence offers free access for clinicians. Check their website for current pricing and any premium features that may require subscription.

faqs.q: How accurate are AI clinical evidence tools?
faqs.a: AI evidence tools vary in accuracy. The best ones cite peer-reviewed sources so you can verify. Always apply clinical judgment - these tools support but don't replace your training and expertise.

faqs.q: What's the difference between OpenEvidence and UpToDate?
faqs.a: UpToDate provides curated expert-written summaries with regular updates. OpenEvidence uses AI to search and synthesize literature on-demand. Both have value; some clinicians use both for different purposes.

faqs.q: Can I use clinical evidence tools during patient visits?
faqs.a: Yes, that's their primary design. Many clinicians use these tools to quickly check treatment options, drug interactions, or guideline recommendations during encounters.

hubs.seo_title: Best AI Scribes for Mental Health Clinicians 2026 | HeyPsych
hubs.meta_description: Compare AI scribes and documentation assistants for therapists and psychiatrists. Ambient note-taking, SOAP note generators, and voice-to-text tools.
hubs.direct_answer: AI scribes like DeepScribe use ambient listening to automatically generate clinical notes from patient encounters. They can save clinicians 1-2 hours of documentation time daily while maintaining note quality.
hubs.intro: Documentation burden is a leading cause of clinician burnout. AI scribes and documentation assistants can listen to your sessions and generate structured notes, freeing you to focus on your patients.

faqs.q: How do AI scribes work for therapy sessions?
faqs.a: AI scribes use ambient listening (with patient consent) to record and transcribe therapy sessions. They then generate structured notes (often SOAP format) that you review and sign. The AI handles transcription and note structure.

faqs.q: Are AI scribes HIPAA compliant?
faqs.a: Reputable AI scribes are HIPAA compliant and offer Business Associate Agreements (BAAs). Always verify compliance and ensure patient consent before recording. Check that PHI isn't used for model training.

faqs.q: Do AI scribes work for psychiatric evaluations?
faqs.a: Yes, many AI scribes are trained on psychiatric and mental health encounters. Some are specifically designed for behavioral health documentation including intake evaluations, therapy notes, and psychiatric assessments.

faqs.q: How much time can AI scribes save?
faqs.a: Clinicians report saving 1-2 hours per day on documentation. The exact savings depend on your current documentation time, note complexity, and how well the AI adapts to your workflow.

faqs.q: What should I look for in an AI scribe?
faqs.a: Key factors: HIPAA compliance with BAA, mental health specialization, EHR integration, note accuracy, customization options, and pricing. Trial periods are valuable for assessing fit with your practice.

hubs.seo_title: Mental Health Billing & Coding Tools 2026 | HeyPsych
hubs.meta_description: Billing and coding tools for mental health practices. Claims submission, CPT coding assistance, prior authorization, and revenue cycle management.
hubs.direct_answer: Mental health billing tools help with claims submission, CPT coding, prior authorization, and revenue cycle management. The right tools can reduce claim denials and speed up reimbursement for therapy and psychiatric services.
hubs.intro: Mental health billing has unique complexities: carve-outs, prior auth requirements, therapy-specific CPT codes, and payer-specific rules. These tools help streamline billing and reduce claim denials.

faqs.q: What billing codes do therapists use most?
faqs.a: Common therapy CPT codes include 90834 (45-min individual), 90837 (60-min individual), 90847 (family therapy), and 90853 (group therapy). Psychiatric codes include 90791 (diagnostic evaluation) and 99213-99215 (E/M with med management).

faqs.q: What causes the most claim denials in mental health?
faqs.a: Common denial reasons: missing prior authorization, incorrect coding, eligibility issues, timely filing, and incomplete documentation. Many denials are preventable with proper verification and coding practices.

faqs.q: Should I bill insurance or go private pay?
faqs.a: Both models have pros and cons. Insurance increases patient access but adds administrative burden and lower reimbursement. Private pay offers higher rates and less paperwork but limits patient access. Many practices use a hybrid model.

faqs.q: What is a clearinghouse and do I need one?
faqs.a: A clearinghouse is an intermediary that submits claims to multiple payers electronically. Most practices benefit from using one (like Availity or Office Ally) as they reduce errors and speed up submissions.

faqs.q: How can I reduce billing administrative time?
faqs.a: Automation helps: EHRs with integrated billing, eligibility verification tools, automated claim scrubbing, and electronic remittance. Some practices outsource billing entirely to specialized services.

hubs.seo_title: Prescribing & Medication Tools for Psychiatrists 2026 | HeyPsych
hubs.meta_description: Medication management tools for psychiatrists and prescribers. Drug interaction checkers, e-prescribing, prior auth tools, and pharmacology references.
hubs.direct_answer: Prescribing support tools include e-prescribing platforms, drug interaction checkers, prior authorization tools, and pharmacology references. These help psychiatrists and prescribers make safer, more efficient medication decisions.
hubs.intro: Psychiatric prescribing involves complex medication interactions, prior authorizations, and monitoring requirements. These tools support safer prescribing and streamline the medication management workflow.

faqs.q: What e-prescribing tools work for controlled substances?
faqs.a: E-prescribing controlled substances (EPCS) requires certified software with identity proofing and two-factor authentication. Most major EHRs offer EPCS. Standalone options include DrFirst and Surescripts-certified platforms.

faqs.q: What drug interaction checkers do psychiatrists use?
faqs.a: Common tools include Epocrates, Lexicomp, Clinical Pharmacology, and EHR-integrated checkers. For psychiatric-specific interactions, consider resources focused on psychotropic medications and CYP450 interactions.

faqs.q: How can I speed up prior authorizations?
faqs.a: Electronic prior auth (ePA) tools integrated with your EHR can reduce PA time significantly. CoverMyMeds and similar platforms connect directly with payers. Some states now require payers to support ePA.

faqs.q: What tools help with medication monitoring?
faqs.a: PDMP (Prescription Drug Monitoring Program) integration, lab tracking for medications requiring monitoring (lithium, clozapine), and automated alerts in your EHR help ensure safe medication management.

faqs.q: Are there AI tools for psychiatric prescribing?
faqs.a: Emerging AI tools offer clinical decision support for medication selection based on patient factors. These should support, not replace, clinical judgment. Evidence for AI prescribing tools in psychiatry is still developing.

hubs.seo_title: EHRs & Practice Management for Mental Health 2026 | HeyPsych
hubs.meta_description: EHRs and practice management tools for therapists and psychiatrists. PracticeQ, SimplePractice, scheduling, telehealth, and practice operations.
hubs.direct_answer: Mental health-specific EHRs like PracticeQ, SimplePractice, and TherapyNotes combine scheduling, documentation, billing, and telehealth in one platform designed for therapy and psychiatric practices.
hubs.intro: Running a mental health practice requires specialized tools. These EHRs and practice management platforms are designed for therapists, psychologists, and psychiatrists with features for scheduling, notes, billing, and telehealth.

faqs.q: What is the best EHR for solo therapists?
faqs.a: SimplePractice and TherapyNotes are popular for solo therapists due to ease of use and all-in-one features. PracticeQ offers more customization. The best choice depends on your specific workflow needs.

faqs.q: What EHR is best for group practices?
faqs.a: Larger practices often choose PracticeQ, Valant, or enterprise solutions. Key factors: multi-provider scheduling, role-based permissions, reporting, and scalable pricing.

faqs.q: Do I need separate telehealth software?
faqs.a: Most modern mental health EHRs include HIPAA-compliant telehealth. Standalone options like Doxy.me work if your EHR lacks telehealth. Integration with your workflow is key.

faqs.q: How do I choose between mental health EHRs?
faqs.a: Consider: ease of documentation, billing features, telehealth quality, patient portal, integrations, pricing model, and customer support. Free trials are valuable for hands-on comparison.

faqs.q: What scheduling features matter for mental health practices?
faqs.a: Key features: recurring appointments, automated reminders (SMS/email), patient self-scheduling, waitlist management, buffer time settings, and calendar integration.

hubs.seo_title: Patient Engagement & Therapy Homework Apps 2026 | HeyPsych
hubs.meta_description: Patient engagement tools for mental health: therapy homework apps, mood trackers, and digital therapeutics to support patients between sessions.
hubs.direct_answer: Patient engagement tools like mood trackers, CBT apps, and digital therapeutics extend therapy between sessions. Some allow clinician monitoring and assignment of exercises, improving treatment outcomes.
hubs.intro: Therapy doesn't stop when the session ends. These tools help patients practice skills, track symptoms, and engage with treatment between visits. Some offer clinician dashboards for monitoring progress.

faqs.q: Can I assign therapy homework through an app?
faqs.a: Some apps allow clinicians to assign specific exercises or modules. Others provide general CBT or mindfulness content. Look for clinician dashboard features if assignment and monitoring are important.

faqs.q: What apps can I recommend for between-session work?
faqs.a: Popular options include mood trackers (Daylio, eMoods), CBT apps (Woebot, Wysa), and meditation apps (Headspace, Calm). Choose based on the patient's needs and your treatment approach.

faqs.q: Are digital therapeutics effective?
faqs.a: FDA-cleared digital therapeutics like reSET and Somryst have clinical trial evidence. Consumer apps vary in evidence quality. Consider the evidence base when recommending tools to patients.

faqs.q: How do I integrate patient apps into treatment?
faqs.a: Start by selecting apps aligned with your treatment approach. Introduce them as homework or skill-building tools. Review patient data or progress in sessions. Adjust recommendations based on engagement.

faqs.q: What about patient privacy with these apps?
faqs.a: Consumer apps aren't typically covered by HIPAA unless there's a BAA. Discuss privacy with patients. Consider whether you need apps with clinician access or are simply recommending self-help tools.
